STRANGE FISH OF THE SEA.

Few boys have been lucky enough to catch a diver with a bent pin and a piece of string; and this younger, who was waiting for tiddlers at Steel Point, Sydney, got the surprise of his life when his line broke and this strange fish emerged. Ineredulty and wonder remained on his face for the rest of the day, as he trailed in the footsteps of the members of the Sydney Microscopical Society in their search for marine specimens. Diver Anderson scoured the sea-floor while the other members explored rock-pools.

new type of air boat; This all Australian flying boat - the wedge - was designed and built in Sydney by Squarey - Leader Wackett. It embodies many novel features, and its trials are being watched with the closest interest. Squarey - Leader Wackett is shown sitting in the stern of the flat-bottomed dingy, which normally is carried on the flying boat.

AUSTRALIAN SHIPBUILDING TRIUMTH: The Ferndale, the second of the Commonwealth Government's 12800 ton steamers to be built at Cockatoo Dockyard (Sydney) was launched on June 1.2th. The Ferndale will be carrying cargo between England and Australia early next year. The christening ceremony was performed by Mrs Earle Page, wife of the Federal Treasurer.
Torrin
AORANGI IN DRY DOCK. The world's largest motor ship was dry-DOCK in Sydney. Photo shows her four propellers.

SYDNEY'S ROOTTOPS: A little known view of Sydney showing Darling Harbor and some of the large warehouses along York and Clarence Streets. The excavation seen almost in the centre of the picture is Wynyard Square which will be one of the stations on the City's Underground Railway now under construction.

ARMISTICE DAY IN SYDNEY The principal ceremony of the 7th Anniversary of Armistice Dayy was held in Martin Place, preceded by a procession through streets of Naval and Military forces. Photos shows: The impressive two minutes silence of Reverence and Homage at eleven o'clock.
SYDNEY HEADS- The entrance to Port Jackson, from the air. Over tonnage aggregating 9,000,000 tons.

MASSACRES IN SLOMONS, IRAS Adelaide lying in the harbor at Malta where natives recently massacred a number of whites. The visit of the Australian warship has already had a salutary effect on the tribes and no more trouble has occurred since her arrival.

SPECIAL SERVICE SQUADRON'S HISTORY MAKING WORLD TOUR. An excellent photograph of the flagship of the squadron, H.M.S. Hood, berthing at Port Melbourne, (Victoria) on its arrival at Melbourne. On the left is the White Ensign floating from the stern of the Light Cruiser Delhi. The powerful little tug's hawser was strained to breaking point by the 44,000 tons of the Hood.

AORANGI IN DRY DOCK, The world's largest motor ship was dry-doiced in Sydney. Photo shows a bow view of the ship.

OUT OF THE HURLY BURLY: yet only 15 minutes by ferry from the business heart of Sydney. Mosman Bay, a never ending paradise to the tired city man is one of the prettiest spots in the world. It will be gaily illuminated at night during the visit of the Duke and Duchess of York who reach Sydney March 26.

Every year, great interest is taken in the Victorian public schools' boat races which are held on the river Yarra at Melbourne. An aerial view of the race is shown, with the crowds of people who witnessed it on the banks of the river. The lines of motor cars may be seen waiting for their owners in one of the avenues close by.

SEA CADRES HAVE THEIR CON-SHIP. The Concord (Sydney, New South Wales) Company of Sea Cadets are probably the only boys in Australia who have their own ship to train and live on. Parents of the cadets and interested residents of Concord recently leased the ship Lindstol, well known in the New Zealand - Australian timber trade and on August 2 she was officially handed over to the boys. Photo shows the Lindstol lying at anchor in the Parramatta River.

CAPTAIN COOK OBJECTED: Early on the morning of Anzac Day, when all Australia was preparing to commemorate the deeds of her men at the war, the Pilot steamer "Captain Cook" was taking the pilot off a German merchantman outward bound from Sydney Harbor. It was too much for the spirit of the great navigator whose bust is the figurehead of the pilot boat. Before anyone realised what was kexpp happening the smaller vessel collided with the German ship head-on. The collision was not serious, but Captain Cook had to be lashed to theowsprit after the encounter.

LAUNCHING THE 'FORDSDALE'. The largest ship constructed in Australia - 12,800 tons was launched and christened the 'Fordsdale' at Cockatoo Dock, Sydney, on June 20. The vessel was built by the Commonwealth Government, to add to its fleet of cargo-carriers many of which are now idle.

SINKING OF H.M.A.S.AUSTRALIA. On Saturday, April 12, in the presence of other ships of the Royal Australian Navy, and after the Royal salute of 21 guns had been given by ships of the visiting British Special Service Squadron, the hull of H.M.A.S.Australia, once the flagship of the Australian Navy, was sunk in 150 fathoms of water, 24 miles off Sydney Heads. The sea-cocks were opened and a hole blown in the bottom, and she capsized and sank in 21 minutes, H.M.A.S.Brisbane firing Royal salute as hull disappeared. The Australia, which was sunk in conformity with the Washington agreement, cost £1,850,000 and was commissioned in 1913. Aerial Photo shows:- The Australia being towed out through Sydney Heads which she entered so proudly in 1913.

SIX MURCH'S CHURSE. The H.M.A.S.melbourne being overhled in Cockstroe Dock (Sydney) just before her departure for six months' service in the Mediterranean with the Royal Navy督军. This visit marks the third association, in peace time, of an Australian cruise with the Royal Navy.

The scrooner Catfish created quite a stir in Sydney by appearing and disappearing at various pints off the coast during a couple of days heavy weather. When she finally struggled into Sydney Harbor, she was declared to hold the record for the slowest voyage from Tasmania to Sydney - 55 days. Photos shown some of the Catfish's desk-cargo of timber.

BUILT IN AUSTRALIA: The Ferndale, the second of this type of cargo vessels built at Cockatoo Government Dockyard Sydney, for the Commonwealth Government, is shown leaving Sydney Harbor for the first time, on her speed trials. The tests proved entirely satisfactory.

GOVERNOR-GENERAL'S WIN. Although the Governor-/general (Lord Stonehaven) has only just arrived in Australia, he has/good fortune in the yacht world. On October 31st the 21ft. class restricted yacht race was won by the Corella (on Sydney Harbor) which, for the first time carried the racing flag of the Governor-General. Photo shows the start of the race.

DOOMED$^{1}$ H.M.A.S.Australia, once the proud flagship of the Australian Navy, as she swings at anchor in Farm Cove, Sydney Harbor, awaiting her doom. Under the Washington agreement she is to be destroyed in February. It has not yet been decided what will be done with the vessel, but there is a strong movement to have her filled with concrete and sunk to form a breakwater at one of the North Coast (N.S.W.) ports. The Federal Government, however, considers that this would probably be construed as a breach of the agreement and the "Australia" will, therefore, almost certainly be sunk at sea.

EVEN THE NAVY FELT IT. The recent hot weather in Sydney affected even the iron discipline of the Navy. These R.A.N. cadets, in a recent muster parade, marched through the city with coats off and sleeves rolled up.

DISMANTLING A BATTLESHIP: Her guns destroyed, her engines% gutted, and her hull sold to the ship-breakers, there is little left of H.M.A.S.Australia at Garden Island (Sydney) to indicate that she was but a couple of years ago the flagship of the Royal Australian Navy. ABANDONING MILSONS POINT: This photograph shows the normal activity at Milsons Pt, the terminus of train, tram, omnibus and ferry services at North Sydney. SIMING OF H.M.A.S. AUSTRALIA. On Saturday, April 12, in the presence of other ships of the Royal Australian Navy, and after the Royal Salute of 21 guns had been given by ships of the visiting British Special Service Square, the hull of H.M.A.S.Australin, once the flagship of the Australian Navy, was sunk in 150 fathoms of water, 24 miles off Sydney Hands. The sea-cocks were opened and a hole blown in the bottom, and sea coopsized and sunk in 21 minutes, H.M.A.S.Brisbane firing Royal salute as mill disappeared. The Australia, which was sunk in conformity with the Washington agreement, cost $21,850,000 and was comprised in 1913. Photo shows: - How hull tips dismarried. Men in boat in foreground are leaving the Australia after having fired the charge and opened the sea-cocks.
